title: SLO-driven token-budget scheduler with KV slab isolation
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: implement an SLO-aware scheduling layer for the continuous batcher that enforces per-customer and global latency SLOs via an explicit token-budget preemption model and a KV cache slab isolation scheme to reduce costly cross-tenant KV eviction. This ticket covers design, implementation, benchmarks, and canary rollout of: (1) a token-budget allocator that gives each inflight request a consumable token budget representing GPU memory + compute entitlement for a sliding window; (2) a preemption mechanism that uses the token budget to decide cooperative vs. forced preemption under contention; and (3) KV cache slab partitioning by tenant/priority band to bound worst-case memory amplification from large KV caches. Motivation: we have observed tail latency spikes during mixed workloads (long-context completions + many small chat requests) where continuous batching saturates GPU memory and causes KV thrashing and expensive kernel context switching. Current global preemption policies are blunt and cause unfair starvation for low-volume tiered customers. The new design aims to (a) preserve p95/p99 latency SLOs for high-priority customers, (b) reduce cross-tenant KV eviction by isolating KV slabs, and (c) improve throughput efficiency by making preemption decisions based on token budgets rather than simple queue age.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler enforces per-tenant token budgets and logs token accounting for every request
KV cache supports slab assignment and eviction metrics exposed by tenant and slab
Under mixed synthetic workload, p95 latency for priority-1 tenants stays <= 200ms and p99 <= 600ms (compared to baseline where p99 > 1.2s)
GPU memory OOMs related to KV cache evictions reduced by >= 80% on our stress test cluster
End-to-end canary on dedicated pool with 5% traffic rollout shows no customer-impacting errors and meets SLOs for 24h
Design doc and code PR merged, and automated regression tests added to CI
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Scoped work; kicked off design doc and spike to measure per-request GPU memory footprint and KV residency by token-window. Matt and Priya ran memprof traces on runtime-ops cluster.

2026-03-07: Spike results: long completions (>=8k tokens) account for 60-70% of active KV entries and cause >2x eviction churn for small chat requests. Baseline p99 tail correlated with KV eviction rate.

2026-03-09: Prototype token-budget allocator implemented as a lightweight object in the batcher that tracks (tokens_remaining, kv_bytes_reserved). Introduced a reclaim path for cooperative cancellation when tokens exhausted. Initial microbench shows reduced queueing for high-priority requests but some throughput drop for background workloads.

2026-03-11: KV slab isolation PoC: added tenant->slab mapping and per-slab LRU with soft limits. Integration test shows slab hit-rate improves by 18% for low-volume tenants under heavy long-completion load.

2026-03-12: Design review with PM and SRE: decided on hybrid preemption semantics (prefer cooperative cancellation; escalate to immediate preempt only if token budget deficit persists beyond a short grace window). Trade-off: cooperative mode reduces unnecessary work loss but can delay enforcement on misbehaving clients.

2026-03-13: Benchmarks: synthetic mix (40% long-completions, 60% short-chat) on rtx-8000-like nodes. Priority-1 p99 improved from 1.25s to 420ms; overall throughput dropped ~6% in worst-case but unit cost per useful token improved by ~9% due to less repeated KV warmups.

2026-03-14: Preparing canary PR and rollout plan. Added feature flag to enable token-budget scheduler and slab isolation independently for safer ramp. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5421
design_decisions: Token budget = estimated GPU work + KV footprint. We derive the budget from request characteristics (expected generated tokens, context length) and runtime-estimated per-token cost by model family.
Initial budgets are conservative and adjusted by adaptive feedback loop from observed service time and KV hit rates (closed-loop controller per model).

Preemption policy: three modes - HINT (no preempt), COOPERATIVE (ask request to yield within grace window), FORCE (drop/evict immediately). Default policy: COOPERATIVE then FORCE on persistent overrun.

KV cache partitioning: use slab isolation with dynamic minor rebalancing. Each tenant/priority band gets a soft slab limit; excess entries spill to global LRU with lower priority. This avoids a single tenant monopolizing KV cache during bursty long completions.
Memory accounting is integrated into the GPU allocator. KV slabs are backed by contiguous GPU allocations where possible to make eviction inexpensive and measurable.
Fairness: implement weighted-token credits. Higher-tier customers get more tokens per window; low-volume customers gain a minimum reserve to avoid starvation.
risks: Incorrect token cost estimation could either be too permissive (leading to tail latency) or too strict (leading to unnecessary request drops and reduced throughput).
Complexity of slab rebalancing could introduce fragmentation and difficult-to-debug memory patterns in the allocator.
Interactions with existing autoscaler and dedicated pool burst policies may create oscillations if token budgets are too aggressive.
Cooperative preemption requires clients (or runtime tasks) to be cancel-safe; some model runtimes don't support graceful checkpointing and will waste work when forced-cancelled.
test_plan: Unit tests for token accounting library and KV slab APIs
Microbench harness: per-model family latency vs tokens under controlled KV hit-rate scenarios
Stress test: mixed synthetic traffic reproducing production contention patterns; assert SLOs and eviction metrics
Shadow canary: enable scheduler flagged in production for 1% of traffic for 48h to collect telemetry without affecting customers
Gradual canary rollout on dedicated pool: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback if p99 regressions occur
Chaos test: artificially inflate KV entries on a tenant to validate slab isolation and prevention of cross-tenant OOMs
metrics_to_monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency by tenant and model
preemption_events (cooperative vs forced) and reason codes
notes: Follow-up: evaluate combining slab isolation with tiered compressed-KV for massive context models to further reduce memory footprint.
PM feedback: ensure user-visible metrics in Console for customers to understand preemption e.g., 'tokens_consumed' and 'preempt_count' per route.
SRE request: add alerting rule when forced preempt rate > 0.5% of requests in a 5m window
